The Healthmate
Communication Core

Every message we send a host, from the first cold hello to the annual re-curation, matched to the asset that travels with it. Built on Master Definition v2, the Healthmate Journey, the Becoming a Healthmate deck and what is live on lifedhealth.com today. Copy, change the bracketed bits, send.

How the library works

Find the condition, not the channel. Each slip names the exact moment it belongs to, the channel that suits it, and the one asset that goes with it. If a moment is not here, that is a gap worth writing a slip for rather than improvising.

Reading a slip

CodeStage letter plus number. Log it against the host so anyone can see what was last sent.
ChannelWhatsApp is the default in this market. Email is for centres, organisers and anything needing a paper trail.
AssetWhat you attach or link. Never more than one per message.
TriggerThe condition that fires the message, and the timing.

Four rules that hold it together

OneOne link per message. lifedhealth.com/become-a-healthmate is the destination; everything else supports it.
TwoEvery message ends with one small next step. Not "let me know", but "shall I send the note?" or "Tuesday 11am or Thursday 4pm?"
ThreePartners, not vendors. A Healthmate is someone we selected, not a supplier we are recruiting. That word choice is a brand lock.
FourNon-clinical, always. No cures, no treatment, no guaranteed outcomes, in any message, ever.

R6Inbound DM: "what is a Healthmate?"Instagram DMPage link
Fires when: someone replies to a post or story asking what this is. Answer in one message, then ask one question.

A Healthmate is a host we have validated and chosen to work with: a practitioner, a centre, a community or an organiser running something real, in person.

You bring the craft and the place. The Lifed team co-creates one program around it, brings the right people to it, and handles discovery, bookings and payment.

The full picture: [lifedhealth.com/become-a-healthmate]. What is it you do, and where?

R7Objection handling, six short answersAnyFAQ card
Fires when: a host raises the standard doubts. Use one at a time. Never send all six.

"What does it cost to join?"
Nothing upfront. No listing fee, no subscription, and no charge for co-creation, curation or marketing. Lifed earns a commission only on a confirmed booking: 20% on residential, 25% on session-based, deducted at settlement rather than invoiced to you.

"I already have my own clients."
Good, and they stay entirely yours. We bring people who do not know you yet, to a program built around what you already do best.

"I do not have time for marketing."
That is the point. Discovery, the program page, photography guidance, bookings and payments sit with Lifed. Your time goes into hosting, which is the part only you can do.

"Do I have to run a fixed format?"
No. You control your calendar. Residential or session-based, and within each there are several formats, from a one-off slot to a weekly series to a pack the guest schedules themselves. We pick the one that suits your work.

"How is this different from a listings site?"
They aggregate. We curate. Every program is shaped with its host and validated against a standard before it goes live, which is why being on Lifed means something to the people who book.

"How long until I am live?"
Most hosts are validated within a day. Co-creating the program takes a few days after that, so about a week from application to bookable.

ComplianceNever answer a "will this cure X" question with a yes. Lifed is non-clinical. Say: programs are wellbeing experiences, not treatment, and we help people before things break rather than after.
R8No reply after the video, one follow-upWhatsAppLive program example
Fires when: five days after R1 or R3 with no response. Send once, then move to A4 timing.

[Name], one thing that usually explains it better than I can.

[Pick the closest live program: a five-session sound and breath series in Fort Kochi at ₹13,999 / a five-day Ayurvedic stay in Puducherry at ₹25,000 / a five-session yoga pack in Kochi at ₹6,250]. That is a real Healthmate, a real price they set themselves, bookable today.

If your work could sit alongside that, I am happy to walk you through it. If not, no trouble at all and I will leave you to it.

STAGE 3

Co-create

Goal: one strong program per Healthmate, built with them, priced by them, in language we can publish.
C1Co-creation session, prep briefWhatsAppCanvas
Fires when: the session is booked. Send 48 hours ahead.

[Name], for our session on [day], come with five things in your head. Nothing to prepare on paper.

1. The one change a person would notice in themselves after time with you
2. How that time actually runs, hour by hour or session by session
3. Who this is genuinely not for
4. The most people you can host well at once
5. What you need in place to run it properly every time

The team builds the program around your answers. About ninety minutes, and you leave with a draft.

Question 3 matters mostA host who can say who it is not for has a real program. A host who says "everyone" needs another session before anything is written.
C2Choosing the format, in plain termsAnyFormat one-pager
Fires when: the host asks what they can list, or is choosing between formats during co-creation.

Two ways to host, and you can run both.

Residential means guests stay with you, with accommodation and meals included. Three to fourteen days is the sweet spot. A guest booking it sees one of two things: "Set dates", which is a dated cohort arriving and leaving together, or "Start any day", where they choose when to arrive inside a window you have open. Most centres start with "Start any day" and add set-date cohorts once demand is proven.

Sessions mean no stay, one to ten sessions typically. A guest sees four options: "Set dates" for specific scheduled dates, "Same time every week" for a weekly slot they keep, "Days in a row" for consecutive days with the same group, or "You pick every session", where they buy a pack and choose their own times.

The weekly slot and the pack are where repeat bookings live, and they are the most reliable income a practitioner can build here. The pack in particular suits busy professionals with unpredictable weeks.

Two vocabularies, kept straightInternally these are Fixed, Flexible, Seasonal, Weekly recurring, Intensive and Flexi. To a host or a guest, use the plain wording above: it is what appears on the site, so it is what they have already read. Note also that residential is 20% and sessions are 25%, so settle the mode before the pricing conversation.
C3Program draft sent for reviewEmailDraft program page
Fires when: the team has written the program from the session. Within two days of it.
Subject: [Program name], first draft for your eyes

Dear [Name],

Here is [Program name] written up: objective, structure, inclusions, group size, and the page as a guest will read it.

Please check three things and only three. Is anything factually wrong. Is anything promised that you cannot deliver every single time, at the stated capacity. And does it sound like you.

Mark it up however you like and send it back by [date]. Nothing goes live without your approval.

Guard rail"Anything you cannot deliver every single time" is the most valuable review question we ask. It is where refund disputes and lukewarm first reviews are prevented.

Joining, listing, co-creation, curation and marketing: no fee

Read it and reply with any correction. If it is right, reply "agreed" and we move to the content day.

Worked example to include if it helpsA five-session series at ₹13,999 means ₹3,500 to Lifed and ₹10,499 to the host, per booking. A five-day residential at ₹25,000 means ₹5,000 and ₹20,000. Show the arithmetic once and the commission conversation is over.

Fires when: terms are agreed and the shoot is scheduled. Send three days ahead.

[Name], for [day], here is what helps.

We will capture the space, your hands at work, one full sequence of the practice, and a short piece to camera answering "why do you do this". Nothing to memorise. We ask, you answer.

Fires when: a host describes their work with a medical or outcome claim. Handle it in the moment, kindly, and never let it reach a page.

[Name], one thing on wording before we publish.

STAGE 4

Curate

Goal: the program clears the standard, and a host who does not clear it first time is reworked with, not rejected.

[Name], [Program name] has cleared the curation check.

It met all five: a clear objective a stranger understands, a sound structure, honest non-clinical language, genuine fit with the people we would guide to it, and deliverable exactly as written, every time, at the stated capacity.

It goes live on [date]. Your share kit reaches you that morning so you can tell your own people first. Being on Lifed means you cleared this bar, and that is the part that protects your reputation as much as ours.

K2One more pass before it goes liveCall, then WhatsAppNone
Fires when: the program does not clear the bar. Call first. This is never framed as a rejection.

[Name], as we spoke, [Program name] needs one more pass before it goes live. Here is exactly what, so nothing is vague:

1. [Criterion, and the specific gap]
2. [Criterion, and the specific gap]

I will rework these with you on [day] and put it back through the same week. Nothing restarts.

Being blunt about why we do this: a weak program that goes live hurts you more than a week's delay does. It books once, gets a lukewarm review, and never really recovers. We would rather spend the week.

The published promise"If it does not clear the bar, we do not reject you and disappear." This slip is where that promise is either kept or quietly broken, so it is worth over-communicating here.
K3Explaining LEWIS to a hostAnyNone
Fires when: a host asks what LEWIS is, or before go-live so they understand how some seekers reach their program.

LEWIS is an optional feature a seeker can use if they would like help choosing. It reflects their wellbeing across nine areas and points them toward programs that fit.

Three things worth knowing. It is non-clinical and never a diagnosis. It is never required, so people can search, browse and book you without it. And it is fit-based, never something you bid on: we do not sell ranking, and we will not push volume at a program that does not suit someone.

What it does for you is quieter and better. The clearer and more honestly described your program is, the more it reaches the right people rather than simply more people.

Language lockNever call LEWIS "AI", "the algorithm", a test, a score or an assessment. It is Lifed's wellbeing intelligence: optional, non-clinical, fit-based.

Corporate groups differ from our usual guests. They arrive as colleagues, some will be reluctant, and punctuality matters more than depth. If that suits you, say yes here and I will send the full brief. If it does not, say so plainly and it changes nothing about our other work together.

Channel lock"Lifed for Business" is a legitimate term in host and B2B conversations and stays out of consumer-facing copy entirely. Employee wellbeing data is never shared with an employer, and never with a host.
G6Dormant Healthmate, re-engagementCall, then WhatsAppNone
Fires when: a Healthmate has not opened dates or responded for 60 days.

[Name], it has been a while and I did not want to let it drift further.

Three possibilities and any of them is fine: this is your busy season, something about the program is not working for you, or your priorities have moved. Tell me which and I will act accordingly.

If it is the second, I would rather rebuild the program with you than watch a good one go quiet.

G7Quality concern, the difficult conversationCall only, then summaryNone
Fires when: a guest reports a real problem, or reviews fall below standard twice. Never open this over text.

[Name], following our call, here is what we agreed so neither of us is working from memory.

What was reported: [factual, specific, no adjectives].
Your account of it: [their side, fairly stated].
What changes before the next booking: [one or two concrete things, with a date].

The reason I am raising it directly is that the curation standard is what protects every Healthmate on Lifed, including you. I would rather fix this with you than quietly stop guiding people to your program.

RuleFacts without adjectives. "Two guests said the session started forty minutes late" is workable. "Guests were unhappy with your professionalism" starts a fight and fixes nothing.
G8Inviting a second programWhatsAppFormat one-pager
Fires when: a host has delivered three or more programs at standard, or has an obvious gap in their calendar.

[Name], [program] is working. I think there is a second one in what you already do.

What I have in mind: [a "same time every week" version for repeat bookings / a pack people schedule themselves, for unpredictable weeks / a "start any day" residential to fill the off-season / a seasonal window for (period)].

Same practice, different shape, and it would fill [the specific gap: your Tuesday evenings, your monsoon months]. Ninety minutes with the team is all it takes to draft it. Shall I book it for [day]?

Where the growth isA second format from an existing, proven Healthmate is cheaper and faster than a new host, and it is the main route to a calendar that is steady year-round rather than feast or famine.
G9Asking a Healthmate for a referralWhatsAppNone
Fires when: a host has just had a good month or a strong review. Ask on the high, never on the flat.

[Name], [the specific good thing that just happened]. Thank you for it.

One ask. We are choosing [number] more Healthmates in [region] this quarter, and the best ones always come from people already in the network.

Is there one person whose work you genuinely respect? Not a favour to them, only someone you would be happy to be listed beside. Send me the name and I will take it from there, and I will tell them you sent me.

Why "one"Asking for one name gets a name. Asking for "anyone you know" gets a promise to think about it.
G10Pausing or parting waysCall, then emailNone
Fires when: either side decides to stop, for any reason.
Subject: [Program name], next steps

Dear [Name],

As discussed, [Program name] comes off Lifed on [date].

Practically: bookings already confirmed will be honoured through [date], your final settlement of ₹[amount] reaches you on the usual weekly schedule by [date], and the photographs and program text are yours to use wherever you wish.

Thank you for the [number] guests you hosted with us. If circumstances change, you would be welcome back without starting from the beginning.

Why this mattersHow hosts leave is what they tell the community. A generous exit costs almost nothing and buys years of goodwill in a small market.

Healthmates · [Month Year]
The memo

Hosting with Lifed

Curated, real-world wellbeing programs — co-created with the people who run them.

What Lifed is. A global platform to book and host curated, real-world wellbeing programs: residential stays and session-based workshops across wellness, functional movement and recovery. We do not relist what already exists. Every program is co-created with the host and validated to a standard before it goes live.

Why it exists. Most help with wellbeing arrives after something has already broken down, and the support that does exist is scattered. At the same time, excellent centres and practitioners stay invisible and seasonal. Lifed closes that gap from both sides.

What a Healthmate is. The host: a practitioner, a centre, a community or an organiser. Partners, not listings. Lifed currently has 50+ curated programs across 10+ locations, and we take a limited number of new Healthmates at a time.

What we ask of you. Identity or business registration. Qualifications, certifications or licences for your practice. Venue details and photographs. Payout details. Where relevant, insurance, safety provisions, a food licence and any permits. Then about ninety minutes for a co-creation session, and half a day for content capture.

What Lifed handles. Program design with you: objective, structure, inclusions, group size and pricing. The written program page, in honest non-clinical language. Photography guidance and imagery. Discovery through search, category browsing and earned placement. Bookings, guest communication and secure payment collection. Weekly settlement to you. Verified reviews. A named contact who stays with you from validation through your first bookings.

The commercials. No joining fee, no listing fee, no subscription, and no charge for co-creation, curation or marketing. You set the guest price; we advise on the market, you decide. Lifed earns a commission only on a confirmed booking: 20% on residential and 25% on session-based, deducted at settlement rather than invoiced to you. Earnings settle weekly to your bank or UPI.

How long it takes. Most hosts are validated within a day. Co-creation takes a few days from there. Live and bookable in about a week.

Where we stand Kerala Startup MissionStartup IndiaKSUM Innovation GrantManorama Elevate S2Sustainability ratedFounded at JIPMER
Lifed is non-clinical. Programs are wellbeing experiences, not treatment, and nothing on Lifed diagnoses or replaces professional care. We ask every Healthmate to hold the same line.

The next step. A short call to understand your work, then a ten-minute application. If validation clears, we design your first program together within days.

[Name], [Role], Lifed
Holobiont Pvt Ltd, Kochi, Kerala
Live Well. For Real.
support@lifedhealth.com · +91 85901 22187
lifedhealth.com/become-a-healthmate

Hosting on Lifed

Two ways to host. Six ways a guest can book it.

Every Lifed program is one category, one delivery mode and one format. The mode decides your terms. The format decides how your calendar behaves, and what a guest sees when they go to book. You can run more than one.

The two modes
ModeWhat it meansTypicalNeeds Commission
Residential Guests stay with you. Accommodation and meals included, multi-day. 3 to 14 days Rooms, food, a day-by-day schedule 20%
Session-based Guests come to you. No stay. Local sessions or workshops. 1 to 10 sessions A space, slots, a repeatable structure 25%
The formats, in both vocabularies
Shown asWhat a guest seesSub-lineCalled internallySuits
Residential Set dates Fixed start and end datesResidential · FixedCentre, Organiser
Residential Start any day You choose when to arriveResidential · Flexible, and Residential · SeasonalCentre, Community
Sessions Set dates Specific scheduled datesSession · FixedPractitioner
Sessions Same time every week A weekly slot you keepSession · Weekly recurringPractitioner, Centre
Sessions Days in a row Consecutive days, same groupSession · IntensivePractitioner, Organiser
Sessions You pick every session Book a pack, choose your own timesSession · FlexiPractitioner, Centre

Rules for whoever sends itNever add a sixth number because it looks good this month, and never drop one because it does not — a changing report card is one nobody trusts. Both bottom lines always filled: if you cannot fill ours, you have not looked at their program this month. Report bookings, earnings, views and ratings, never what the program did for anyone's health. Two consecutive months at zero is not a report card situation; it is a call, and then a rework.

Host-facing only, and one source of truthCommission figures never go into a consumer channel or a public post. If the deck, the terms email, the format one-pager or the film ever change a number, this card changes the same day — a host who sees two different figures stops believing both.

Who becomes a Healthmate

Four kinds of host. One standard.

Partners, not listings. Whichever one you are, the program is built with you and validated before it goes live.

Practitioners Teachers, therapists, coaches and guides who run the sessions themselves. Usually a weekly slot, or a pack the guest schedules.
Centres Retreats, ayurveda centres and studios with rooms, food and a team. Usually residential, starting with "start any day".
Communities Groups already gathering people around movement, food or the outdoors. A structure and a calendar, without losing what makes them theirs.
Organisers People who put programs together with other people's venues and practitioners. Set-date cohorts and days in a row.
Not sure which one you are? Tell us what a normal week looks like and we will place you. Most people who ask turn out to be running two of the four already.
Where it goesInto the Healthmate page as its own section, since every message now names these four. Into cold outreach as the second image after the explainer video. And into the memo's forwarding chain, because a programming head reading it needs to place their own organisation somewhere in the first ten seconds.

Hosting with Lifed

A note for prospective Healthmates · [Month Year] · Live Well. For Real.

What Lifed is. Lifed is a global platform to book and host curated, real-world wellbeing programs: residential stays and session-based workshops across wellness, functional movement and recovery. We do not relist what already exists. Every program is co-created with the host and validated to a standard before it goes live.

Why it exists. Most help with wellbeing arrives after something has already broken down, and the support that does exist is scattered. At the same time, excellent centres and practitioners stay invisible and seasonal. Lifed closes that gap from both sides.

What a Healthmate is. The host: a practitioner, a centre, a community or an organiser. Partners, not listings. Lifed currently has 50+ curated programs across 10+ locations, and we take a limited number of new Healthmates at a time.

What we ask of you. Identity or business registration. Qualifications, certifications or licences for your practice. Venue details and photographs. Payout details. Where relevant, insurance, safety provisions, a food licence and any permits. Then about ninety minutes for a co-creation session, and half a day for content capture.

What Lifed handles. Program design with you: objective, structure, inclusions, group size and pricing. The written program page, in honest non-clinical language. Photography guidance and imagery. Discovery through search, category browsing and earned placement. Bookings, guest communication and secure payment collection. Weekly settlement to you. Verified reviews. A named contact who stays with you from validation through your first bookings.

The commercials. No joining fee, no listing fee, no subscription, and no charge for co-creation, curation or marketing. You set the guest price; we advise on the market, you decide. Lifed earns a commission only on a confirmed booking: 20% on residential and 25% on session-based, deducted at settlement rather than invoiced to you. Earnings settle weekly to your bank or UPI.

How long it takes. Most hosts are validated within a day. Co-creation takes a few days from there. Live and bookable in about a week.

Where we stand. Recognised by Kerala Startup Mission and Startup India. KSUM Innovation Grant winner. Featured on Manorama Online Elevate Season 2. Sustainability rated. Founded at JIPMER, Pondicherry, around one question: why do we only help people after they break.

One important note. Lifed is non-clinical. Programs are wellbeing experiences, not treatment, and nothing on Lifed diagnoses or replaces professional care. We ask every Healthmate to hold the same line.

The next step. A short call to understand your work, then a ten-minute application. If validation clears, we design your first program together within days.

Before this ships

Five things worth fixing first

These came out of putting the deck, the definition docs and the live site side by side. Each one is small, and each one shows up in a host conversation eventually.

1. The timeline contradicts itself across three places

The site says validated in one day and live in about a week. The deck says validated within two days and live by day 10. The Journey doc says approved in one day and published in one week. This library uses the site version, because that is what a host has already read before you speak to them. Pick one and change the other two.

2. "Genuine wellbeing outcomes" sits on the wrong side of your own guardrail

The host FAQ on the site defines curated as vetting for quality, safety and genuine wellbeing outcomes. Your own rule is that outcome measurement is rolling out and is never described as finished. Suggested rewrite: vetted for a clear objective, a sound structure, honest non-clinical language and genuine fit.

3. Confirm which Healthmate stories are real before they go into sales

The deck labels its Healthmate story an illustrative composite, while the site carries a named practitioner testimonial with a video. Your own site rule is that a story appears only after attendance is confirmed and permission is given. Worth confirming written consent and factual accuracy for anything the outreach messages point to, because a host who discovers a composite was presented as a peer will not stay.

4. The live program list needs a pass before you send hosts to it

Several programs appear more than once, some multi-day residential programs are tagged as day programs, and at least one carries a location outside India. R8 sends prospective hosts to look at live listings as proof, so this list is now a sales asset. Half a day of cleanup protects both that message and your search visibility.

5. The site hero and the locked tagline are not the same line

The locked tagline is "Live Well. For Real." The homepage leads with a functional booking line instead. Your own marketing kit flags this as a founder decision still open. Whichever way it goes, the memo, the video end frame and the poster should all carry the same one.

The position, in one line

The seeker is the hero. The Healthmate is the guide. Lifed is what brought them to each other. Every message to a host should make that host feel chosen, not recruited.
